118599.subject: Chemistry

118599.sol: Benzene sulphonic acid contains the sulfonate (-SO 3 H) functional group.

118812.sol: The Lucas test is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols based on their reactivity with Lucas reagent (concentrated HCl and anhydrous ZnCl₂ ). 120828.subject: Chemistry
120828.text: What makes it difficult to define vitamins based on their chemical structure?
options: They all belong to the same chemical class.
They are synthesized by the human body.
120828.sol: Vitamins have diverse chemical structures, which makes it challenging to define them based solely on their chemical characteristics.

121019.subject: Chemistry
121019.text: Identify the correct statement regarding the properties of enzymes.
options: Enzymes increase the activation energy of biochemical processes to accelerate them.
Enzymes are primarily composed of complex polysaccharides.
Enzymes act as biocatalysts and are required only in very small quantities.
A single enzyme can efficiently catalyze many unrelated biochemical reactions.
121019.sol: Enzymes are biocatalysts that are required in very small quantities to catalyze biochemical reactions. The other statements are incorrect because: - Enzymes lower (not increase) the activation energy of biochemical processes. - Almost all enzymes are globular proteins, not polysaccharides. - Enzymes are highly specific; a particular enzyme generally catalyzes only one specific reaction or acts on a specific substrate. Answer: Enzymes act as biocatalysts and are required only in very small quantities.

121440.subject: Botany
121440.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Before the introduction of five kingdom classification bacteria, Fungi, Mosses all were categorised under kingdom Plantae Reason: Bacteria, Fungi, Mosses all possessed cell walls
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
121440.sol: Bacteria, Fungi and Mosses were categorised under kingdom Plantae as they all contain cell walls similar to plants.

archaebacteria that contains protein homologous to eukaryotic core histones
archaebacteria that lack any histones resembling those found in eukaryotes but whose DNA is negatively superco

121627.subject: Botany
121627.text: The bacteria Pseudomonas aeruginosa is useful because of its ability to
options: transfer genes from one plant to another
decompose a variety of organic compounds
fix atmospheric nitrogen in the soil
produce a wide variety of antibiotics.
121627.sol: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a Gram-negative, aerobic rod belonging to the bacterial family Pseudomonadaceae. These bacteria are common inhabitants of soil water. They occur regularly on the surfaces of plants and occassionally on the surfaces of animals. The bacterium will grow in the absence of O ₂ if NO ₃ is available as a respiratory electron acceptor. 121648.sol: Prions are disease causing proteinaceous molecules. These lack nucleic acid and are formed due to abnormal folding of proteins.

121841.subject: Botany
121841.text: From where is the pollen grain released in gymnosperms?
121841.sol: Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, in gymnosperms the male and the female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence. They remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophytes. The pollen grain is released from the microsporangium. They are carried in air currents and come in contact with the opening of the ovules borne on megasporophylls. The pollen tube carrying the male gametes grows towards archegonia in the ovules and discharges their contents near the mouth of the archegonia. Following

122194.subject: Botany
122194.text: What is the common name for members of the phylum that sponges belong to?
122194.sol: The common name for members of the phylum that sponges belong to is Porifera. Sponges are generally marine animals and are typically found in marine environments.Sponges have a water transport or canal system. Water enters through minute pores (ostia) in the body wall into a central cavity, spongocoel, from where it goes out through the osculum. This pathway of water transport is helpful in food gathering, respiratory exchange and removal of waste. Choanocytes or collar cells line the spongocoel and the canals. Dig

122676.subject: Botany
122676.sol: Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of insects. It opens at the junction of midgut and hindgut (ileum) in cockroach. Malpighian tubules absorb excretory substances from haemolymph and fat bodies and pass into the proctodaeum. The excretory product of insects is uric acid related with water conservation. 122730.subject: Botany
122730.text: In which type of inflorescence does the main axis continue to grow?
122730.sol: A flower is a modified shoot wherein the shoot apical meristem changes to floral meristem. Internodes do not elongate and the axis gets condensed. The arrangement of flowers on the floral axis is termed as inflorescence. 123391.subject: Botany
123391.text: Mesophyll Components Descriptions A. Palisade Parenchyma 1. Surrounding vascular bundles B. Spongy Parenchyma 2. Oval or round cells with large intercellular spaces C. Epidermal Cells 3. Cells covering the leaf surface D. Bundle Sheath Cells 4. Elongated cells arranged vertically
123391.sol: The palisade parenchyma consists of elongated cells arranged vertically, the spongy parenchyma has oval or round cells with large intercellular spaces, epidermal cells cover the leaf surface, and bundle sheath cells surround vascular bundles.

123578.subject: Botany
123578.text: What is the most dramatic period of the cell cycle?
123578.sol: This is the most dramatic period of the cell cycle , involving a major reorganisation of virtually all components of the cell. Since the number of chromosomes in the parent and progeny cells is the same, it is also called as equational division. Though for convenience mitosis has been divided into four stages of nuclear division (karyokinesis), it is very essential to understand that cell division is a progressive process and very clear-cut lines cannot be drawn between various stages.

124929.subject: Botany
124929.text: What strategy does the plant cell use to make the energy from glucose useful?
options: Store all the energy as heat
Catabolize glucose in several small steps
Release all the energy in one step
124929.sol: The strategy that the plant cell uses is to catabolize the glucose molecule in such a way that not all the liberated energy goes out as heat. 125017.text: What is the net gain of ATP molecules for each molecule of glucose in fermentation?
125017.sol: • Fermentation accounts for only a partial breakdown of glucose whereas in aerobic respiration it is completely degraded to CO2 and H2O. • In fermentation there is a net gain of only two molecules of ATP for each molecule of glucose degraded to pyruvic acid whereas many more molecules of ATP are generated under aerobic conditions. • NADH is oxidized to NAD+ rather slowly in fermentation, however the reaction is very vigorous in case of aerobic respiration

125297.subject: Botany
125297.text: What else is photosynthesis responsible for besides being the primary source of food?
options: Release of oxygen into the atmosphere
125297.sol: All animals including human beings depend on plants for their food. Have you ever wondered from where plants get their food? Green plants, in fact, have to make or rather synthesise the food they need and all other organisms depend on them for their needs. The green plants make or rather synthesise the food they need through photosynthesis and are therefore called autotrophs. 125306.text: What conclusion did Priestley draw about burning candles and animals that breathe air?
options: They do not affect the air.

125614.text: A specific chemical inhibitor completely blocks the functioning of the photosystem whose reaction centre has an absorption maximum at 680 nm. Which of the following physiological processes will be directly and immediately halted as a result?
options: Splitting of water and oxygen evolution
125614.sol: The photosystem with an absorption maximum at 680 nm is Photosystem II (PS II). PS II is physically associated with the water-splitting complex located on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane. This complex is responsible for the photolysis of water, which releases electrons, protons, and oxygen. Therefore, blocking PS II directly halts the splitting of water and the subsequent evolution of oxygen. 125777.subject: Botany
125777.text: What structures develop from the floral primordium?
125777.sol: Much before the actual flower is seen on a plant, the decision that the plant is going to flower has taken place. Several hormonal and structural changes are initiated which lead to the differentiation and further development of the floral primordium. Inflorescences are formed which bear the floral buds and then the flowers. In the flower the male and female reproductive structures, the androecium and the gynoecium differentiate and develop. You would recollect that the androecium consists of a whorl of stamens rep

126188.subject: Botany
126188.text: Read the following statements regarding the development of a flower from a vegetative shoot: (A) The shoot apical meristem transforms into the floral meristem. (B) The internodes of the floral axis elongate significantly to accommodate the various floral whorls. (C) Floral appendages are produced laterally at successive nodes instead of leaves. 126188.sol: Statement (A) is correct as a flower is a modified shoot where the shoot apical meristem changes into a floral meristem. Statement (B) is incorrect because during floral induction, the internodes do not elongate; instead, the axis gets condensed. Statement (C) is correct as the condensed apex produces different kinds of floral appendages laterally at successive nodes instead of leaves. Statement (D) is incorrect because floral appendages are morphologically considered modified leaves, not modified lateral branches.

126196.subject: Botany
126196.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true
126196.sol: Assertion (A) is true because in cereals such as rice and wheat, pollen grains lose viability within 30 minutes of their release. 126660.sol: Primary structure (A) refers to the linear sequence of amino acids (II) in a polypeptide chain. Secondary structure (B) involves α-helix and β-sheet formation (III) stabilized by hydrogen bonds. Tertiary structure (C) is the 3D folding (I) of a single polypeptide chain due to interactions between R groups. Quaternary structure (D) is the association of multiple polypeptide chains (IV) into a functional protein.

128764.subject: Zoology
128764.text: Which body fluid is commonly used by higher organisms including humans for transporting materials within the body?
128764.sol: More complex organisms use special fluids within their bodies to transport such materials. Blood is the most commonly used body fluid by most of the higher organisms including humans for this purpose . Another body fluid, lymph, also helps in the transport of certain substances.

128869.subject: Zoology

128869.sol: The entire heart is made of cardiac muscles. The walls of ventricles are much thicker than that of the atria. A patch of this tissue is present in the right upper corner of the right atrium called the sino-atrial node (SAN). 129446.subject: Zoology
129446.text: Which of the following is the part of mid brain of rabbit?
129446.sol: The dorsal part of mid brain (mesencephalon) is in the form of two pairs (i.e., four) of spherical optic lobes (corpora quadrigemina) located behind the pineal body optic lobes are reduced merely as reflex centres of visual and auditory.

129464.subject: Zoology
129464.text: What type of excretory structures are found in most of the invertebrates?
129464.sol: : A survey of animal kingdom presents a variety of excretory structures. In most of the invertebrates, these structures are simple tubular forms whereas vertebrates have complex tubular organs called kidneys. Some of these structures are mentioned here. Protonephridia or flame cells are the excretory structures in Platyhelminthes (Flatworms, e.g., Planaria), rotifers, some annelids and the cephalochordate – Amphioxus. 129577.subject: Zoology
129577.text: What is the primary function of sweat produced by sweat glands?

To provide a protective oily covering for the skin
To facilitate a cooling effect on the body surface
To remove glucose from the body
129577.sol: The sweat and sebaceous glands in the skin can eliminate certain substances through their secretions. Sweat produced by the sweat glands is a watery fluid containing NaCl, small amounts of urea, lactic acid, etc. Though the primary function of sweat is to facilitate a cooling effect on the body surface, it also helps in the removal of some of the wastes mentioned above. 130947.subject: Zoology
130947.text: What happens to the mammary glands of the female during pregnancy?
130947.sol: The mammary glands of the female undergo differentiation during pregnancy and starts producing milk towards the end of pregnancy by the process called lactation. This helps the mother in feeding the newborn. The milk produced during the initial few days of lactation is called colostrum which contains several antibodies absolutely essential to develop resistance for the new-born babies. Breast-feeding during the initial period of infant growth is recommended by doctors for bringing up a healthy baby.

133389.sol: The exaggerated response of the immune system to certain antigens present in the environment is called allergy. Common examples of allergens are mites in dust, pollens, animal dander, etc. Symptoms of allergic reactions include sneezing, watery eyes, running nose and difficulty in breathing. 97416.subject: Botany
97416.text: Analyze the given life cycle of plants and select the plants which represent such a life cycle.
97416.sol: The diploid sporophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic, independent phase of the plant. The gametophytic phase is represented by the single to the few-celled haploid gametophyte. This type of life cycle is termed as diplontic. An alga, Fucus sp., represents this pattern. In addition, all seed-bearing plants, i.e., Gymnosperms and Angiosperms, follow this pattern with some variations wherein the gametophytic phase is few to multi-celled.
